seed_inputs.title: Mirror Flow Matching with Heavy-Tailed Priors for Generative Modeling on Convex Domains
seed_inputs.source_note: Seed paper on mirror flow matching, convex-domain generation, heavy-tailed dual distributions, Student-t priors, and Wasserstein error bounds.

seed_inputs.title: Total Variation Rates for Riemannian Flow Matching
seed_inputs.source_note: Seed paper on nonasymptotic TV rates for learned and discretized Riemannian flow matching on compact and Hadamard manifolds.

domain: mathematical foundations for learned generative samplers

core_problems.problem: Establish nonasymptotic sampling error bounds for flow matching samplers when the learned velocity field is discretized by Euler-type ODE integration.

evidence.note: Theorem 7 decomposes Wasserstein error into discretization, learned velocity approximation, and early stopping terms.
Theorem 1 gives a TV bound separating step-size and estimation errors on compact manifolds.

core_problems.problem: Extend flow matching from Euclidean space to geometry-constrained domains such as convex bodies, manifolds, hyperspheres, and SPD manifolds while preserving feasible trajectories.

evidence.note: The paper frames constrained target support and mirror maps as the route to feasible flow matching.
The paper formulates RFM with tangent vector fields, geodesic interpolation, logarithm maps, and parallel transport.

core_problems.problem: Control velocity-field regularity near the terminal time and under heavy-tailed or noncompact target distributions.

evidence.note: The paper identifies heavy-tailed dual distributions, Gaussian-prior mismatch, and the need for spatial and temporal regularity.
The paper explains the fragile cancellation near t=1 and motivates early stopping.

core_problems.problem: Design geometry-aware transformations or priors that make constrained or noncompact flow matching analytically well posed.

evidence.note: The modified mirror map is designed to transform constrained distributions, preserve moments, and transfer dual guarantees to primal guarantees.
The SPD case uses a Riemannian Gaussian prior and exponential moment assumptions to obtain polynomial iteration complexity.

core_problems.problem: Find reusable proof frameworks that convert local vector-field, score, divergence, curvature, and moment bounds into global sampling guarantees.

evidence.note: Theorem 7 proof couples exact and discretized flows, uses Young's inequality, recurrence control, and an early-stopping term.
The paper's proof sketch centers on a TV differential identity through divergence and score terms.

methods: Riemannian flow matching with geodesic interpolation
coupling exact and numerical ODE flows
compact versus Hadamard manifold case splitting
assumptions: learned vector field is epsilon-accurate in value, and sometimes in derivative or divergence
early stopping time T is strictly less than 1 to avoid terminal-time stiffness
target distribution satisfies finite moment, polynomial tail, boundary layer, or exponential moment conditions depending on geometry
mirror map is strongly convex or has a dual metric that controls primal Wasserstein distance
Riemannian manifold has bounded curvature, positive injectivity radius or Hadamard/global chart structure as needed
population flow-matching vector field has spatial, temporal, divergence, and score regularity
Euler step size is small enough for exponential-map invertibility and controlled interpolation
for noncompact manifolds, uniform pointwise bounds may be replaced by expectation-level regularity
proof_patterns: transport-stability differential inequality: differentiate TV or distance between two flows and bound by vector-field mismatch terms
exact-vs-discretized flow coupling: initialize two processes together and track error accumulation under Euler discretization
Young inequality error splitting: convert inner products into squared flow error plus discretization or estimation residuals
Gronwall or recurrence unrolling: propagate one-step bounds into terminal nonasymptotic error rates
early stopping decomposition: split terminal sampling error into approximation-to-T error plus T-to-1 bias
conditional-expectation derivative control: bound derivatives of velocity fields expressed as conditional expectations
moment/tail-to-regularity transfer: turn tail, boundary layer, or exponential moment assumptions into finite regularity constants
dual-to-primal guarantee transfer: prove an error bound in a transformed space and pull it back through a metric or isometry
geometric Euler interpolation: turn a discrete manifold Euler method into a continuous-time ODE using parallel transport and inverse exponential maps
score-divergence decomposition: reduce TV error to score regularity, vector-field mismatch, and divergence mismatch
curvature comparison bound: use comparison theorems or Jacobi-field estimates to control derivatives of Exp/Log and parallel transport
case split by geometry: handle compact manifolds with uniform bounds and Hadamard/noncompact manifolds with expectation-level bounds

user_interest_hypotheses.hypothesis: The user is likely interested in theoretical, proof-heavy work on generative samplers rather than empirical model-design papers.
user_interest_hypotheses.why: Both seed papers emphasize nonasymptotic convergence, velocity-field regularity, discretization, and proof machinery more than experiments.

user_interest_hypotheses.hypothesis: The user may want reusable proof-pattern skills for analyzing learned ODE samplers under geometry, tail, and discretization complications.
user_interest_hypotheses.why: The shared proof motifs are TV/Wasserstein stability, early stopping, coupling, regularity verification, and geometry-dependent bounds.

user_interest_hypotheses.hypothesis: The user's search should include adjacent work on probability-flow ODEs, stochastic interpolants, score-based generative modeling, Riemannian diffusion, and sampling on manifolds.
user_interest_hypotheses.why: The seed papers repeatedly position themselves against Euclidean FM, probability flow ODEs, Riemannian diffusion, and geometric sampling analyses.

user_interest_hypotheses.hypothesis: Potential innovation may come from improving exponential-in-Lipschitz or high-dimensional polynomial constants, weakening moment/tail assumptions, or extending the geometry classes.
user_interest_hypotheses.why: Both papers expose technical bottlenecks in constants, terminal-time singularity, moment assumptions, and curvature-induced growth.

negative_preferences: pure empirical generative modeling papers without convergence or regularity analysis
generic diffusion or flow matching surveys that do not provide reusable proof techniques
papers focused only on architecture or benchmark performance without mathematical guarantees
unconstrained Euclidean-only flow matching unless it introduces a proof method transferable to geometric or constrained domains
manifold learning applications that do not address sampling error, ODE discretization, or geometric regularity
